answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Compass maker drawn chart proof filed with the coast register changes that arithmetic: each drawn chart is a decade of logged surveys plus a signed guild record, so a farm must calibrate a hundred real compasses by hand, so the mesa for each fake is paid in the real world. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the garden of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one. The summit is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
